subject: How to avoid loading a file.

messages.author: e4bb8d219f9f74fd
messages.subject: How to avoid loading a file.
parts:
Hi
I created a web based tool that uses RApache. My web tool is working
perfectly except that it is having some efficiency issues. I am trying
to explain what I need and whether it is possible or not.

Suppose I am doing following calculations in R
1. dataFile = read.csv("testFolder/dataFile.csv", header=TRUE);
2. doCalculations(dataFile);

Every time a user opens the page, both of the lines above will be
executed. Executing line 1 takes around 30 second that is too much
while calculation takes just 3 seconds in my case.

Loading the same file for each user is something which I want to avoid
and I guess there might be some way to skip this step.

Is it possible to write code and some how avoid loading the file? Can
"RSourceOnStartup" or "REvalOnStarup" help me somehow? And how to
receive "dataFile"?

Thanks a lot.
Fahim

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: How to avoid loading a file.
parts:
Well, you can save CSV file to R binary format (.RData, .rda), and load it via REvalOnStartup. If your data is generated dynamically (via some script or smth), you should convert it to binary format, hence load it. If you're emotionally attached to CSV format, you may want to provide colClasses argument in read.csv function. It will speed up whole process, since you will skip looping over each column to determine appropriate column class.

Also, take a look at this link: http://stackoverflow.com/q/4756989/457898

Hi Aleksander,
Thanks a lot for your reply.

My Csv files are generated  once every 3 months and I do not care whether it is in csv format or .Rdata format, I just want my work to be done. I can do the same work in mysql but due to the lack of functionalities in MySQL I resorted to Rapache and R. So basically this tool will be  substitute of a tool based on mysql based system.  

I need to include the following lines in REvalOnStartup

filenames = list.files(path = "/home/fahim/webRugit/mm9/outData", pattern = '.Rdata$', all.files = FALSE, full.names = TRUE, ignore.case = FALSE)
for ( i in 1: length(filenames))
    {   
    x= filenames[i]
    y = unlist(strsplit(x, '/', fixed = TRUE))
    fname = strsplit(y[length(y)], '.', fixed=TRUE)[[1]][1]
    load(file = x)
    assign(fname, dataFile)   #assign into corresponding output variables;    
    }


Putting these codes in a file and then including the file in RSourceOnStartup, works well but the first page (index page) takes too long to load as it loads all the files in the memory.  This is real time consuming and no user wants to wait for minutes to load the  first page.

So I wanted to give REvalOnStartup a try and see whether it improves the load time or not. But the real problem in using the above code with REvalOnStartup is that it shows error when I insert these codes into the config file as REvalOnStartup takes only one argument at a time.
.
"Syntax error on line 6 of /etc/apache2/httpd.conf:
REvalOnStartup takes one argument, R expressions to evaluate on start."

1. How can I format the above code so that REvalOnStartup can accept it??

2. If somehow it works, then will loading time of the page improve??
Or putting it other way, I am in need of some way to load these files when apache starts.  When a user opens the page, it directly access the server memory and do not load these files again.

Thanks and regards
Fahim
